Suspected Bomb Threats Target Seven Flights Across Europe

04 Nov 2026, 12:31 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

2 min read

Key takeawaysSeven passenger aircraft across Europe, including two departing from the UK, were subjected to security inspections following a series of suspected bomb threats. Authorities across multiple nations launched investigations into the incidents, while the UK government characterized the threats as malicious hoaxes.

Overview of European Aviation Incidents

Seven passenger aircraft across Europe, including two departing from the UK, were subjected to security inspections following a series of suspected bomb threats. Authorities across multiple nations launched investigations into the incidents, while the UK government characterized the threats as malicious hoaxes.

Affected Flights and Responses

  • Rome, Italy: Two Ryanair flights originating from Dublin and Lisbon were searched after landing at Fiumicino airport following anonymous tips. Airport sources confirmed no explosives were found. The Dublin flight received an escort from the Italian Air Force prior to landing.
  • Murcia, Spain: A Ryanair flight from Manchester underwent inspection by a bomb squad and fire services upon landing. Passengers reported remaining on the runway before being escorted away by police.
  • Warsaw, Poland: Two flights heading to Warsaw were affected, including a London Heathrow service that diverted to Modlin airport, briefly causing its closure. A Scandinavian Airlines flight from Copenhagen landed as scheduled.
  • Sofia, Bulgaria: Bulgarian Transport Minister Georgi Peev stated that two incoming flights from Bergamo and Dublin faced threats. Border police reported receiving an email concerning an improvised explosive device, which triggered standard protocols and an operational headquarters.

Official Reactions and Expert Insights

  • Government Stance: The UK government stated it maintains a robust aviation security system with established protocols for addressing potential and hoax threats.
  • Co-ordination: While official confirmation of a direct link between the cases is pending, cross-border authorities are co-operating to determine if the events formed a coordinated airspace disruption.
  • Aviation Protocols: Aviation safety experts note that crews and ground operators treat all threats as genuine until proven otherwise. Procedures often involve quiet onboard searches, potential flight diversions to isolated stands, and comprehensive checks by explosive ordnance disposal teams upon landing.

Practical Implications and Verification

Passengers traveling across European routes may experience schedule adjustments or heightened security protocols. Travelers can verify flight statuses directly through official airline channels or aviation authorities before heading to airports.
